name: Vauxhall Spring Gardens
notes: Major renovation under Jonathan Tyers 1728-32. Peak popularity 1730s-1790s.

name: Ranelagh Gardens
notes: Chelsea. Rotunda opened 1742. Closed and demolished 1805. Cannot appear in texts pre-1742.

name: Marylebone Gardens
notes: Closed 1778. Replaced by housing. Cannot appear in texts post-1778.

name: The Pantheon
notes: Oxford Street. Burned 1792; rebuilt as theatre 1795. Cannot appear pre-1772.

name: Almack's Assembly Rooms
notes: King Street St James's. Later Willis's Rooms. Cannot appear pre-1765.

name: Drury Lane Theatre
notes: Current building opened 1794 after fire. Pre-1794 texts refer to earlier structure.

name: Covent Garden Theatre
notes: Burned 1808; rebuilt 1809. Pre-1808 texts refer to earlier structure.

name: King's Theatre Haymarket
notes: Opera house. Burned 1789; rebuilt 1790.

name: St James's Park
notes: Stable throughout the period.

name: Hyde Park
notes: Stable throughout. Rotten Row a key social promenade.

name: Grosvenor Square
notes: Major aristocratic address. Developed 1720s-1730s. Cannot appear pre-1725.

name: Hanover Square
notes: Developed from 1714. Key early Georgian address.

name: Berkeley Square
notes: Developed 1730s-1740s. Gardens laid out 1739.

name: St James's Square
notes: Aristocratic address stable throughout.

name: The Strand
notes: Major commercial and social thoroughfare. Stable throughout.

name: Covent Garden Piazza
notes: Market and social space stable throughout.

name: Spring Gardens (Charing Cross)
notes: Older pleasure garden near Charing Cross. Distinct from Vauxhall.

name: White's Club
notes: St James's Street. Oldest gentlemen's club. Stable throughout.

name: Boodle's Club
notes: St James's Street. Cannot appear pre-1762.

name: Brooks's Club
notes: St James's Street. Cannot appear pre-1764.

name: The Tower of London
notes: Stable landmark throughout.

name: St Paul's Cathedral
notes: Wren's cathedral completed 1710.

name: Westminster Abbey
notes: Stable landmark throughout.

name: Portman Square
notes: Developed from 1764. Home House (notable address) 1775.

name: Portland Place
notes: Developed from 1778. Cannot appear in earlier texts.

name: Bedford Square
notes: Bloomsbury. Developed 1775. Cannot appear pre-1775.

name: Lower Assembly Rooms (Harrison's)
notes: Also known as Lindsey's Rooms. The rooms in pre-1771 Bath fiction. Burned 1820.

name: Upper Assembly Rooms (New Rooms)
notes: Opened October 1771. These are Austen's rooms in Northanger Abbey. Cannot appear pre-1771.

name: The Pump Room
notes: Current building 1796. Earlier versions from 1706. Major social hub throughout.

name: The Circus
notes: Designed by John Wood the Elder 1754; completed after his death 1768. Cannot appear pre-1768.

name: Royal Crescent
notes: Built 1767-1774. Cannot appear in texts set before construction.

name: Pulteney Bridge
notes: Designed Robert Adam. Cannot appear pre-1774.

name: Sydney Gardens
notes: Pleasure gardens. Austen's favourite walk. Cannot appear pre-1795.

name: Queen Square
notes: John Wood the Elder. Completed 1736. Key address in mid-century Bath fiction.

name: Milsom Street
notes: Principal shopping street from 1761. Cannot appear pre-1761.

name: Bath Abbey
notes: Stable landmark throughout.

name: North Parade
notes: Promenade. Developed 1740. Smollett's characters walk here.

name: South Parade
notes: Developed 1743. Cannot appear pre-1743.

name: Bond Street
notes: Old and New Bond Street. Principal shopping and fashionable promenade of the West End. Stable throughout.

name: Pall Mall
notes: Major street between St James's and Charing Cross. Clubs galleries print shops. Stable throughout.

name: Piccadilly
notes: Major thoroughfare from Piccadilly Circus to Hyde Park Corner. Stable throughout.

name: St James's Street
notes: Gentlemen's clubs wine merchants. Heart of St James's. Stable throughout.

name: Fleet Street
notes: Booksellers printers and lawyers. Legal and literary thoroughfare. Stable throughout.

name: Cheapside
notes: Principal City commercial street. Drapers mercers goldsmiths. Stable throughout.

name: Oxford Street
notes: Known as Oxford Road pre-c.1740. Shopping street from 1760s. The Pantheon opened here 1772.

name: Ludgate Hill
notes: City booksellers and publishers near St Paul's. Stable throughout.

name: Cornhill
notes: City banking and insurance district. Royal Exchange nearby. Stable throughout.

name: Charing Cross
notes: Junction of Strand/Whitehall/Northumberland Avenue. Stable throughout.

name: Leicester Fields (Square)
notes: Known as Leicester Fields until c.1670. Fashionable early 18c; declined mid-century.

name: Cavendish Square
notes: Developed from 1717. Key address for upper-middle professional ranks.

name: Harley Street
notes: Developed from 1757. Fashionable medical and professional address.

name: Brook Street
notes: Mayfair. Developed 1720s. Stable thereafter.

name: Don Saltero's Coffee House
notes: Cheyne Walk Chelsea. Curiosity cabinet and coffee house. Frequented by Smollett. Proposed by the Branghtons in Evelina as a vulgar excursion.

name: White-Conduit House
notes: Islington. Pleasure garden and cricket ground. Lower-middling social register.

name: Bagnigge Wells
notes: Clerkenwell. Mineral spring gardens. Popular with tradespeople and servants.

name: Mother Red Cap's
notes: Camden Town tavern. Lower-class excursion destination. Evelina's vulgar alternatives cluster.

name: Will's Coffee House
notes: Russell Street Covent Garden. Dryden's house. Literary centre 1680s-1720s. Declined after Addison.

name: Button's Coffee House
notes: Russell Street Covent Garden. Addison and Steele's house. Whig literary centre.

name: Tom's Coffee House
notes: Russell Street Covent Garden. Subscription house. Active through to 1780s.

name: Slaughter's Coffee House
notes: St Martin's Lane. Artists and chess players. Active throughout.

name: Lloyd's Coffee House
notes: Tower Street then Royal Exchange from 1774. Insurance underwriters.

name: Chapter Coffee House
notes: Paternoster Row near St Paul's. Booksellers and publishers. Active throughout.

name: Garraway's Coffee House
notes: Exchange Alley. Auctions and financial news. Active throughout.

name: The City of London
notes: The square mile. Commercial and financial heart. Contrasted with West End throughout the period.

name: Bloomsbury
notes: Inner northern district. Developed progressively through 18c.

name: Holborn
notes: Legal district. Inns of Court. Stable throughout.

name: Soho
notes: Mixed bohemian district. Huguenot quarter. Stable throughout.

name: Southwark (the Borough)
notes: South bank. Coaching inns Borough High Street debtors prison.

name: Mayfair
notes: Aristocratic West End district. Developed through 18c. Contrasted with City.

name: Gay Street
notes: Connecting Queen Square to the Circus. Built 1734.

name: Cheap Street
notes: Main Bath shopping street. Distinct from London's Cheapside. Stable throughout.

name: Argyle Street
notes: Connects Pulteney Bridge to Laura Place. Part of Bathwick Estate development.

name: Pulteney Street
notes: Grand main street of Bathwick Estate. Cannot appear pre-1789.

name: Newgate Prison
notes: Primary criminal prison of London; adjacent to the Sessions House. Rebuilt 1770-78 (Architects: George Dance the Younger).

name: Fleet Prison
notes: Debtors' prison on the east bank of the Fleet River. Demolished 1844.

name: Marshalsea Prison
notes: Debtors' prison in Southwark. Site now marked in Borough High Street. Cannot appear post-1842.

name: Bridewell Prison
notes: House of correction near Blackfriars Bridge. Originally a royal palace.

name: King's Bench Prison
notes: Debtors' and misdemeanour prison in Southwark Borough.

name: Tothill Fields Bridewell
notes: Westminster house of correction. Site now occupied by HM Prison Belmarsh predecessor.

name: Old Bailey Courthouse
notes: The Sessions House on Old Bailey street; Central Criminal Court from 1907. Adjacent to Newgate Prison.

name: Bow Street Magistrates Court
notes: Founded by Henry Fielding 1739; home of the Bow Street Runners.

name: Smithfield Market
notes: Livestock and meat market; notorious for smell and noise. West Smithfield area.

name: Billingsgate Fish Market
notes: Fish market on Lower Thames Street below London Bridge. Notorious for coarse language and smell.

name: Leadenhall Market
notes: Poultry and general produce market in the City.

name: Covent Garden Market
notes: Fruit and vegetable market; distinct from the Theatre and Piazza entries.

name: St Giles / Seven Dials
notes: Dense slum district; large Irish population. Centre of Seven Dials rookery.

name: Whitechapel
notes: East End district; mixed immigrant population; extensive street trade.

name: Spitalfields
notes: Huguenot weaver district; silk industry; became increasingly impoverished late 18c.

name: Wapping
notes: Riverside district; sailors and dockhands; Execution Dock for pirates.

name: Cheapside
notes: Major commercial thoroughfare through the City of London.

name: Holborn
notes: Mixed district merging lawyers' quarter (Inns of Court) with dense residential areas.

name: Fleet Street
notes: Print trade and taverns; connects City to Temple Bar.

name: Southwark / Borough
notes: South bank district; tanneries; brewing; Bankside entertainment.

name: Tyburn Gallows
notes: Public execution site at the north-east corner of Hyde Park (near modern Marble Arch). Cannot appear post-1783.

name: Newgate Gallows
notes: Public executions moved outside Newgate Prison after 1783. Cannot appear pre-1783.
